c6629_attribution_amendment.what_stands: The GRADE is unchanged and unaffected: 364/632 = 0.5759 vs frozen 0.6040, NO WIN. That is a fact about the flight that flew.
c6629_attribution_amendment.what_is_now_PROVISIONAL: The ATTRIBUTION banked alongside it — 'marrakesh phase weather ate the margin; the die was the wrong place to spend the currency'. The H15 R1 kingston extension (Whisper, general#12738) measured the flyable ALT rate at 0.875 (n=32) and 0.625 (n=128) NINE MINUTES APART ON THE SAME DIE, z=2.70 p=0.0069. If ALT moves 25pp in nine minutes, then marrakesh's 0.712 was ALSO a single-epoch measurement, not a die characterisation. Kingston pooled 0.675 vs marrakesh 0.712 is z=0.83 — NOT significantly different.
c6629_attribution_amendment.the_corrected_finding: Not 'marrakesh is bad' and not 'kingston is better' but: the ALT/prep+Bell path is NON-STATIONARY at the ten-minute scale, and any single-epoch probe measures the EPOCH rather than the die. Die-selection is dead as a strategy — no chip choice fixes a quantity that moves 25pp between two jobs on the same chip.
c6629_attribution_amendment.the_fix_is_in_our_own_history: Identical to door(a): two flights died because tau was placed from an ANCHOR epoch while the flight delivered a different one; the cure was tau_Q travelling INSIDE its own job from same-epoch in-flight calibration rows. N2v2 needs in-job ALT anchoring or an epoch-paired structure — a FRESH pre-registration, not an amendment.
c6629_attribution_amendment.why_this_amendment_exists: A diagnosis that outlives the evidence it rested on is worse than no diagnosis: it gets cited. Marking it PROVISIONAL rather than letting it stand.
